candidate_sentence_map.S1: Tallinna Vesi reported improved financial performance in 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Group revenue increased 11.4% to €72.48 million, supported by 6.9% growth in water-services revenue to €62.31 million and a 62.0% increase in construction-services revenue to €8.46 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Private-customer revenue in the main service area rose 18.3% to €31.84 million, driven by higher consumption and tariff changes.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Business-customer revenue declined 2.7% to €16.76 million following reductions in business tariffs introduced to harmonise private and business prices.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Revenue from customers outside the main service area increased 13.8% to €7.71 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Costs of goods and services sold grew 12.0% to €42.96 million, mainly because construction-services costs increased 74.5% to €7.13 million, staff costs rose 6.8% to €11.45 million, and depreciation and amortisation increased 11.9% to €9.08 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Direct production costs were broadly unchanged at €9.90 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Electricity costs fell 6.9% to €4.37 million, primarily because the combined heat and power plant at Paljassaare produced electricity for internal consumption.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Chemicals costs increased 5.8%, while pollution taxes rose 21.4% because of higher rates and usage volumes.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: Gross profit increased 10.5% to €29.52 million, and operating profit rose 11.8% to €21.22 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: The operating margin was broadly stable at 29.27%, compared with 29.17% in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: Net financial expense declined to €3.78 million from €4.20 million, mainly due to lower Euribor rates.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: Profit before tax increased 18.0% to €17.43 million, while net profit rose 7.2% to €14.24 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Net profit growth was moderated by the higher income tax rate on dividend payments.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: Earnings per share increased from €0.66 to €0.71.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: Fixed-asset investment reached €55.74 million, compared with €49.53 million in 2024, and total assets increased to €364.57 million from €313.84 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: The investment programme was supported by additional borrowing: outstanding loans rose to €160 million from €118 million, increasing the debt-to-assets ratio from 61.71% to 66.02%.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: Operating cash flow improved to €30.83 million from €26.25 million, while year-end cash increased to €11.29 million from €3.59 million after €45.15 million of investing outflows and €10.6 million of dividends paid.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: Operational developments included commissioning the combined heat and power plant, which produced all treatment-plant heat and 43.8% of electricity consumption at the wastewater plant and main pumping station.
candidate_sentence_map.S21: The company laid or reconstructed 45.1 kilometres of pipes, expanded smart-meter installation beyond 80% of customers, and reported fewer sewer blockages and water emergencies.
candidate_sentence_map.S22: Watercom also achieved record turnover and profits as Estonia’s construction market recovered.
candidate_sentence_map.S23: The group retained a €6.02 million provision for tariff-related third-party claims, with five actions totalling €14.67 million still unresolved.

evaluation.label: Generally yes
evaluation.justification: K1, K2, K3, K4, and K6 are fully represented with supporting sentences covering core material meanings. K5 is missing entirely (no mention of drinking water quality compliance, Green Company award, stormwater systems, or climate targets). K7 is missing (no dividend policy details or shareholder payout). K8 is missing (no 2026 strategic priorities). The summary captures most high-importance financial and operational developments but omits key environmental achievements and future strategic directions, resulting in a 'Generally yes' assessment.
